chunks: Allah (may He have mercy on him) narrated to us, Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Bahr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what they narrate that Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, created Adam in His Image; he said: It is a newly created image, Allah chose it and selected it over all other different images, so He attributed it to Himself just as He attributed the Ka'bah to Himself and the Spirit to Himself.
"And I breathed into him from My Spirit"

key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: The Ka'bah (used as an example of attribution)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah created Adam in His Image according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that 'His Image' refers to a distinct, created form selected by Allah and attributed to Him by metaphor, akin to how the Ka'bah or the Spirit are ascribed to God, thereby preserving divine transcendence from physical embodiment. This interpretation aligns with the Shia doctrine of *tanzih* (divine incomparability), rejecting literal anthropomorphism while affirming the reality of Adam's unique creation. The narration underscores that divine attributes are often linguistic attributions rather than essential qualities, a key principle in Shia kalām.
